newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's CCU sees Q1 earnings rising.
newsitem.headline: Chile's CCU sees Q1 earnings rising.

text.p: Chile's largest bewery Compania Cervecerias Unidas said it expects its first quarter earnings to be stronger than last year due to rising demand for beer in Chile and Argentine.
"All our operating units were better in January 1997 than in January 1996," general manager Francisco Perez Mackenna told reporters during a tour of the plant.
"I expect that the first quarter is not only better, but that (sales) are more diversified."
Figures for the company's 1996 first quarter results were not immediately available.
CCU has over 80 percent of the Chilean beer market and owns two breweries in Santa Fe and Salta in Argentina. In Chile, it also owns winery San Pedro.
The company has noted an improvement in beer sales since October after months of flat orders, he said.
"In the last quarter beer sales volumes grew at four percent a year compared with the last quarter of 1995," said Perez.
"This rate of growth was repeated in the first quarter of 1997."
Wine exports have also grown steeply in recent months, he added.
